label: mid-sequence m/x/s/i/1/t/p input in sequences starting with z/3/e/b/j/h
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.8% of activation mass), at positions 1-6. It peaks at t=3-4 and never fires at t=0. Within that range it prefers first occurrences of a small set of input tokens: m (6.9x lift), x, s, i, 1, and to a lesser degree t and p. It is much stronger when the sequence starts with z, 3, e or b (also j or h), and when z sits early in the prefix. The top examples look like e z ... [x], e z c 1 [m], 3 3 j 3 x [m]. Previous tokens q, 1 or x also raise the rate. It is essentially silent at the delimiter and during the copy phase, and on repeated tokens (in_first=0 gives 0.1x). This looks like a conjunction of the current token with features of the prefix held in hidden state, and no simple predicate captures it. The best predicate reached only F1 around 0.41 on dev (precision 0.37, recall 0.47, mass recall 0.61). Magnitude is larger for the predicted cases: coverage rises with activation quartile. The large lower-magnitude remainder fires on other tokens and prefixes.
